p.src: Good books can help. A serious book on logic, judgment, or critical thinking is not merely information; it is a mirror. en: This is why seeing the good in others can feel like a rebirth. The same world becomes richer. The people around you have not changed much. Your access to them has changed. Where you once saw threats, you now see models. Where you once saw reasons to complain, you now see warnings. Where you once saw rivals, you now see data.

p.src: And occasionally, where you once saw an enemy, you may discover a teacher.

u.src: And occasionally, where you once saw an enemy, you may discover a teacher.
en: And occasionally, where you once saw an enemy, you may discover a teacher.

p.src: A Private Exercise

u.src: A Private Exercise
en: A Private Exercise

p.src: This chapter asks for an uncomfortable exercise. It does not need to be public. It should be written.

u.src: This chapter asks for an uncomfortable exercise. It does not need to be public. It should be written.
en: This chapter asks for an uncomfortable exercise. It does not need to be public. It should be written.

p.src: Choose a notebook, or a dedicated section of a notebook, for this one practice: recording the moments when you cannot bear to see the good in others.

u.src: Choose a notebook, or a dedicated section of a notebook, for this one practice: recording the moments when you cannot bear to see the good in others.
en: Choose a notebook, or a dedicated section of a notebook, for this one practice: recording the moments when you cannot bear to see the good in others.

p.src: Write down the name or situation. Then answer:

u.src: Write down the name or situation. Then answer:
en: Write down the name or situation. Then answer:

p.src: What exactly bothers me about this person?

u.src: What exactly bothers me about this person?
en: What exactly bothers me about this person?

p.src: What good quality am I refusing to admit?

u.src: What good quality am I refusing to admit?
en: What good quality am I refusing to admit?

p.src: Why does that quality threaten me?

u.src: Why does that quality threaten me?
en: Why does that quality threaten me?

p.src: What can I learn from it?

u.src: What can I learn from it?
en: What can I learn from it?

p.src: What weakness in me is being exposed?

u.src: What weakness in me is being exposed?
en: What weakness in me is being exposed?

p.src: What action would turn this discomfort into growth?

u.src: What action would turn this discomfort into growth?
en: What action would turn this discomfort into growth?

p.src: Also ask a harder question:

u.src: Also ask a harder question:
en: Also ask a harder question:

p.src: What important lesson have I learned from someone I dislike?

u.src: What important lesson have I learned from someone I dislike?
en: What important lesson have I learned from someone I dislike?

p.src: If you can answer this honestly, your attention is becoming freer.

u.src: If you can answer this honestly, your attention is becoming freer.
en: If you can answer this honestly, your attention is becoming freer.

p.src: The person you dislike may still be untrustworthy. He may still be wrong in many areas. You may still need distance, boundaries, or refusal. None of that cancels the practice. Accuracy is not approval. Learning is not submission. Seeing clearly is not surrender.

p.src: The Final Shift

u.src: The Final Shift
en: The Final Shift

p.src: People who cannot see the good in others are often terrified that others will see the bad in them.

u.src: People who cannot see the good in others are often terrified that others will see the bad in them.
en: People who cannot see the good in others are often terrified that others will see the bad in them.

p.src: This is the hidden symmetry. The person who constantly judges is usually afraid of being judged. The person who erases others’ strengths often fears that his own weaknesses will erase him. The person trapped in comparison cannot rest because he imagines everyone else is comparing in the same cruel way.

u.src: This is the hidden symmetry. The person who constantly judges is usually afraid of being judged. The person who erases others’ strengths often fears that his own weaknesses will erase him. The person trapped in comparison cannot rest because he imagines everyone else is comparing in the same cruel way.
en: This is the hidden symmetry. The person who constantly judges is usually afraid of being judged. The person who erases others’ strengths often fears that his own weaknesses will erase him. The person trapped in comparison cannot rest because he imagines everyone else is comparing in the same cruel way.

p.src: The exit is not to pretend that weakness does not exist. The exit is to accept a more complete reality:

u.src: The exit is not to pretend that weakness does not exist. The exit is to accept a more complete reality:
en: The exit is not to pretend that weakness does not exist. The exit is to accept a more complete reality:

p.src: Every person has strengths and weaknesses. So do I.

u.src: Every person has strengths and weaknesses. So do I.
en: Every person has strengths and weaknesses. So do I.

p.src: From there, life becomes simpler.

u.src: From there, life becomes simpler.
en: From there, life becomes simpler.

p.src: Other people’s strengths are available for study. Other people’s weaknesses are available as warnings. My strengths are available for building. My weaknesses are available for repair.

u.src: Other people’s strengths are available for study. Other people’s weaknesses are available as warnings. My strengths are available for building. My weaknesses are available for repair.
en: Other people’s strengths are available for study. Other people’s weaknesses are available as warnings. My strengths are available for building. My weaknesses are available for repair.

p.src: No drama is required.

u.src: No drama is required.
en: No drama is required.

p.src: The instruction is severe but liberating:

u.src: The instruction is severe but liberating:
en: The instruction is severe but liberating:

p.src: Proving yourself is not important. Growth is important. If growth becomes real, proof will take care of itself.

u.src: Proving yourself is not important. Growth is important. If growth becomes real, proof will take care of itself.
en: Proving yourself is not important. Growth is important. If growth becomes real, proof will take care of itself.

p.src: To see the good in others is not merely to become kinder. It is to recover a large part of the world as usable material. It is to stop paying attention to rank and begin paying attention to reality. It is to build the inner position from which wealth freedom becomes possible: I can grow, and you can grow; I can be good, and you can be good; your excellence does not reduce my future.

p.src: The person who reaches that position has not escaped competition by becoming weak. He has escaped useless competition by becoming stronger.
